newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mobil plans Altona CDU turnaround, FCC replacement.
newsitem.headline: Mobil plans Altona CDU turnaround, FCC replacement.

text.p: Mobil Australia Ltd plans to shut its 55,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) No.3 at its Altona refinery for maintenance for a month around the middle of the year, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"There is a broad window from May to August for timings but we don't actually have dates," the spokesman said. "There are a number of (internal) issues that have to be resolved first."
The Altona refinery is near Melbourne and is currently operating at 118,000 bpd. The refinery has two CDUs, including one with 63,000 bpd capacity.
One of the internal issues relates to Mobil's plan to permanently shutdown of a 24,000-bpd thermal catalytic cracker (TCC) and replace it with a fluid catalytic cracker of the same capacity.
This procedure will also take a month and some other secondary units will come down around it, but the sequence of the shutdown has yet to be finalised, the spokesman said.
The new FCC was due for completion sometime in April to May, he said.
The company does not plan any major refinery turnarounds at it 75,000-bpd refinery at Adelaide because a major shutdown was carried out last year, the spokesman said.
A separate company source said the 75,000-bpd CDU would be shut for a week while a 27,000-bpd reformer was closed for catalytic regeneration for about a week in the second half of the year.
